headline: MacIntyre's precision offense carries Tennessee past Michigan State's passing attack
body: George MacIntyre dissected Michigan State's secondary with surgical accuracy, completing 23 of 27 passes for 262 yards and three touchdowns in Tennessee's 42-27 victory on Saturday. The performance exemplified a stark contrast in offensive efficiency: Tennessee's ball security and decisiveness against Michigan State's willingness to air it out and live with the consequences. MacIntyre's 85.2 completion percentage and three touchdown passes on minimal attempts left little room for Michigan State to establish rhythm, even as the Spartan offense accumulated 284 passing yards through the air.

The turning point came in Tennessee's ability to sustain drives through the run game despite modest rushing totals. Baker's 10 carries provided enough ground presence to prevent Michigan State from teeing off on every third-and-long, while Dodson's 102 receiving yards on seven receptions gave the Volunteers consistent chunk plays that moved the chains and ate clock. Michigan State's Bernard and Glass kept the Spartans competitive with a balanced effort, but Glass's 28-for-45 completion line hinted at stalling drives and third-down pressure that ultimately determined field position.

Tennessee's defense made enough plays when it mattered. Spillman's sack and four tackles symbolized a unit that wasn't dominant but created just enough disruption to keep Michigan State from mounting a sustained comeback. The single fumble lost by Tennessee proved inconsequential in the context of MacIntyre's control of the game, whereas Michigan State's inability to generate turnovers meant the Spartans had to execute nearly flawlessly—a bar they couldn't consistently reach against a team that simply made fewer mistakes.
turningPoint: MacIntyre's three touchdown passes in the first half established a 28-14 halftime lead that Michigan State never closed despite Glass and the passing game keeping pace statistically in the second half.

unsungHero.name: Dodson
unsungHero.why: While MacIntyre earned Player of the Game accolades, Dodson's 102 yards on seven receptions were the connective tissue that allowed Tennessee's offense to sustain drives and control tempo, freeing up the ground game and keeping Michigan State's defense on its heels throughout the afternoon.
